title: Contribute a fix you can't push
prompt:
You cloned `open-themes/vite-themes` directly, fixed a typo on a branch called `fix-readme-typo`, and ran `git push -u origin fix-readme-typo`. GitHub answers:

```text
ERROR: Permission to open-themes/vite-themes.git denied to maya-okafor.
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
```

What's the right way to get your fix to the maintainers without redoing the work?
hints: The error isn't about your SSH key; GitHub knows exactly who you are.
You need a copy of the repository on GitHub that you are allowed to push to.
Your existing clone can talk to more than one remote.
explanation: You don't have write access to `open-themes/vite-themes`, so no credential will make that push work. Fork it on GitHub, which creates `maya-okafor/vite-themes`. In your existing clone, rename the current `origin` to `upstream` (`git remote rename origin upstream`) and add your fork as `origin` (`git remote add origin git@github.com:maya-okafor/vite-themes.git`). Then `git push -u origin fix-readme-typo` and open a pull request from your fork's branch to the original's `main`. Your commit is reused as is.

a.text: Generate a new SSH key and add it to your account, then push again.
a.why: The message names your username, so authentication worked. The problem is permission: you aren't a collaborator on that repository.

b.why: Forcing changes how a branch is overwritten, not whether you're allowed to write. The push is still denied.

c.text: Email the maintainers and ask them to add you as a collaborator so you can push your branch.
c.why: Maintainers don't grant write access for a typo fix. Forks exist so anyone can contribute without it.

d.text: Fork it on GitHub, make the original `upstream` and your fork `origin` in this clone, push the branch to your fork, and open a pull request to the original.
d.why: Correct. Your fork is a repository you can push to, and a pull request from it is how changes reach a project you don't own.
